sources.name: WHO — Investing in treatment for depression and anxiety leads to fourfold return
Chisholm et al. — Scaling-up treatment of depression and anxiety, The Lancet Psychiatry

categories.methodology: Approximate annual cost (~USD 9.8 billion) of scaling up treatment for depression and anxiety — the WHO/World Bank estimate of US$147 billion over 2016-2030 across 36 countries (~80% of the global burden of these disorders), divided across the 15-year window (Chisholm et al., Lancet Psychiatry 2016).

sources.name: UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report — annual financing gap of almost $100 billion
UNESCO GEM Report — Can countries afford their national SDG 4 benchmarks? (full report)

categories.methodology: Average annual financing gap of ~USD 97 billion (2023-2030) for 79 low- and lower-middle-income countries to reach their national SDG 4 targets (universal pre-primary, primary and secondary education), per the UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report.

One year of the World Health Organization's entire approved programme budget: the 2024-2025 biennium budget of US$6.83 billion divided by two, ~USD 3.42 billion/year (WHO Programme Budget 2024-2025, resolution WHA76.1).

sources.name: PATH / Policy Cures Research — Bridging the gaps in malaria R&D

categories.methodology: Average annual global investment in malaria research and development (~USD 673 million, 2014-2016 average; basic research plus product development), per PATH / Policy Cures Research 'Bridging the gaps in malaria R&D' — about US$100 million short of target.

sources.name: Sriudomporn et al. — Achieving Immunization Agenda 2030 coverage targets for 14 pathogens, Vaccine X
Gavi, The Vaccine Alliance — Resource Mobilisation Process

categories.methodology: Estimated ~USD 27 billion per year — the full annual cost of delivering a routine immunisation schedule against 14 pathogens to every child across 194 countries (~USD 269.8 billion total over 2021-2030, vaccine product plus delivery), per Sriudomporn et al., Vaccine X 2022.

sources.name: Laborde et al. — Ending hunger: science must stop neglecting smallholder farmers, Nature

categories.methodology: Average additional ~USD 33 billion/year ($14B donors + $19B LMIC governments) through 2030 to end hunger (SDG 2), per Ceres2030 (IFPRI/IISD/Cornell).

sources.name: World Bank — The Costs of Meeting the 2030 SDG Targets on Drinking Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene

categories.methodology: ~USD 37.6 billion/year capital investment for universal safely-managed drinking water (SDG 6.1 component), per the World Bank's SDG 6 costing study (Hutton & Varughese 2016).
